subject: Clarify output vs service license — procurement & legal checklist
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Turner <amelia.turner@fintechx.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify output vs service license — procurement & legal checklist

Hi Laura / Connor,

FinTechX (Amelia, cc'd) sent back an annotated MSA + order form that contains a few significant redlines around output ownership, retraining / model use, and a perpetual feedback license. They want clarity on what we can accept given Dedicated + Hosted options.

Attached: FTX_MSA_redline_20260717.pdf (annotated MSA), orderform-exhibitB-draft.docx

High-level asks from my side:
- Can we accept their proposed language giving them "exclusive ownership of outputs" for customer-created prompts? If not, what compromise language removes the appearance of assignment but gives productization comfort?
- They insist on a perpetual unlimited feedback license that allows them to ship model improvements to third parties. We typically push back — what’s the narrowest fallback language we can offer (time-boxed, purpose-limited, non-exclusive)?
- They are asking to prohibit any internal use of generated outputs for retraining ("strict opt-out"). For Dedicated customers we often agree operationally, but hosted terms are different. Need a short guidance we can share with procurement today so they can proceed.

Timing: procurement is asking for a clear legal position by EOD Monday (20th) so they can finalize the order form. Can you weigh in with suggested redline text or a short summary note we can send Amelia? If a call would help, I can set up a 30-min sync Monday morning.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Turner <amelia.turner@fintechx.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify output vs service license — procurement & legal checklist

Thanks Rishi — looping in my initial read here. Quick take up front: we should not accept an assignment of outputs; we can offer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive license back to the customer for their internal business use and downstream productization if they pay for a productization add-on. For feedback rights, a time-limited, purpose-limited license (e.g., two years; limited to improving the Redwood service) is reasonable.

Detailed suggestions (draft language below) — Amelia, sharing so we're transparent:
1) Output ownership: change to "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer-Provided Content. Redwood grants Customer a non-exclusive, royalty-free right to use Generated Output for its internal business operations; productization rights require an executed Productization Addendum."
2) Feedback license: counter with "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use feedback submitted by Customer for the purpose of improving Redwood services for a period of 24 months, after which Redwood must either obtain renew consent or cease using that feedback for model training."
3) Training / retraining: for Hosted API customers, we keep standard opt-in for training; for Dedicated, we can pass an operational commitment to not use outputs for Redwood training unless the customer explicitly opts in. We'll need Procurement to map the customer's account to the Dedicated offering in the order form to operationalize that.

We'll also need to flag telemetry/telemetry retention in Exhibit B — Connor, can you confirm whether FinTechX requested extended telemetry retention or export controls?

If Amelia needs different language, propose a 30-min call Monday 09:00–11:00 PT. I can have a short redline ready by EOD.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Amelia Turner <amelia.turner@fintechx.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@fintechx.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify output vs service license — procurement & legal checklist

Laura — thanks for the quick initial read. A few clarifications from our side to explain why we pushed the stronger language:
- We are a regulated payments provider. Our legal team needs clarity that outputs derived from our confidential prompts cannot be used by vendor for their commercial models or redistributed; that is a showstopper for us.
- The productization add-on model is workable if the scope and pricing are clear; Samir (cc) will own the procurement details.
- Regarding the feedback license, our ask is not to give unlimited rights to Redwood to retrain on PII-sensitive prompts. Could we do a carveout: Redwood may use anonymized, aggregate telemetry for quality improvements, but raw prompts or outputs may not be used for training without explicit written consent?

We can do a call Monday at 10:00 PT if that works for legal to walk through wording. We appreciate the suggested alternatives.

Regards,
Amelia Turner
Head of Procurement | FinTechX
amelia.turner@fintechx.com

Amelia / team — thanks for the rapid replies and context. Confirming next steps and owners so procurement can close the deal Monday afternoon: 

Action items:
- Laura: prepare a redline MSA that replaces the proposed assignment with the non-exclusive output license language and inserts the 24-month feedback license with an explicit carveout for PII and raw prompts. (Deliverable: redline PDF)
- Connor: update the Order Form to include a Productization Addendum option and flag this account as Dedicated-capable operationally so we can offer the training opt-out. (Deliverable: updated orderform-exhibitB-draft.docx)
- Amelia / Samir: confirm whether FinTechX is requesting telemetry export or extended retention. If yes, Laura will scope Exhibit B changes accordingly.

Call: 30-min sync Monday 10:00 PT (I will create the invite). If legal needs more time, Laura, we can push signature to Tue but procurement asked for Monday close — please advise.

I attached the MSA redline they sent (FTX_MSA_redline_20260717.pdf) and the current order form excerpt. I’ll circulate the calendar invite now.
